This article will explore the challenges faced by farmers on the ground and analyse whether the measures in place are sufficient to reverse the sector 's declining fortunes . <h> The @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ vital component of Kenya 's economy , with around 15 -- 20% of its land classified as arable . However , only 7 -- 8% is deemed high-quality for cultivation . By the end of the 2010s , approximately 75% of the population relied on farming for their livelihoods , a decline from 80% in 1980 . <p> Despite the limited land available for agriculture in Kenya -- less than 8% for crops and feed and less than 20% overall suitable for agriculture -- Kenya is a leader in tea and coffee production . The country also ranks as the third-largest exporter of fresh produce , including cabbages , tomatoes , onions , and mangoes . <h> How important is agriculture to the Kenyan economy ? <p> In terms of economic contribution , agriculture immensely impacts Kenya 's GDP . In the second quarter of 2024 , the sector 's contribution to GDP reached 539,507 million KES , an increase from 516,295 million KES in the first quarter . The average agricultural GDP from 2009 to 2024 stands at 382,058.16 million KES . <p> In 2023 , agriculture accounted for @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ or 17% of the total GDP from all sectors . This followed a $20.21 billion contribution in 2022 , which represented a 9.5% rise from the previous year . <p> In 2021 , agriculture 's GDP share was one of the highest in Africa at 22.4% . In contrast , the tourism sector generated $2.7 billion from international arrivals in 2023 , marking a substantial 32% increase from 2022 . <p> However , agriculture in Kenya is predominantly subsistence-based , with productivity stagnating in recent years despite ongoing population growth . Only about 20% of the country 's land is suitable for farming , and optimal yields remain unachieved . <p> The agricultural industry mainly comprises small to medium-sized farmers , who typically own between 0.2 to 3 hectares of land . Small-scale farming constitutes 75% of the total market and accounts for up to 70% of marketed agricultural output . <p> The agricultural sector is also highly dependent on bimodal rainfall patterns . Approximately 80% of the country is classified as arid or semi-arid , averaging only 400 mm of annual rainfall . Droughts are frequent and can impact @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ faced by Kenyan farmers <p> Farmers in Kenya encounter various interconnected challenges that hinder their livelihoods and economic contributions . Recognizing these issues is essential for determining effective interventions to assist farmers and rejuvenate the agricultural sector . <p> In an exclusive interview with Tuko.co.ke , Geoffrey Kavita , an agronomist who has practised across Kenya , both in the private and public sector , said that in his practice , he has observed that in Kenya , there is a significant gap in agricultural knowledge among farmers , which has had a negative impact on both productivity and profitability in agribusinesses , as well as on food security . <p> These knowledge gaps are evident across various stages of crop production , from seed selection and land preparation to crop protection , nutrition , and post-harvest handling . As an agronomist , I often meet seasoned farmers , and one common issue I observe is that many use the same fertilizer feeding regimes for all their crops , regardless of crop family . It takes considerable effort and training to help them understand that applying a feeding regime tailored @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ <p> While various agricultural technologies exist in Kenya , their adoption remains limited and has not reached mainstream use . Additionally , both geographic and demographic factors hinder progress . Many rural areas , particularly those distant from the capital , lack reliable mobile and Internet connectivity . Although Kenya 's ICT Development Index shows year-on-year improvement , the pace is insufficient to match that of other countries . <h> 2 . Lack of enough funding opportunities <p> Farmers have long raised concerns that Kenya 's agricultural funding opportunities are minimal and less reliable . Many lament inadequate funding frameworks and channels for the agricultural sector -- it has not been clear how Kenyan farmers can access government resources . As a result , many have relied on informal financing mechanisms , which are often unable to meet the sector 's needs in terms of both quality and quantity of financial support . <p> According to the 2019 FinAccess survey , only about 3.2% of farmers in Kenya utilise formal borrowing to fund their agricultural activities . Instead , they primarily rely on selling assets , alternative income sources , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ highlights that approximately 8.5 million individuals in Kenya engage in some form of agricultural activity , with 6.3 million relying on it as their primary source of income . <p> 69% of these farmers focus on food crop production . Insufficient access to proper financing for essential areas such as inputs , working capital , mechanisation , and risk management significantly hampers productivity across various agricultural value chains compared to leading global producers . <h> How has this affected farmers ? <p> The accessibility of credit often influences farmers ' choice of capital sources . Many find themselves limited in their options , compelled to accept whatever financing is available . This raises the question of whether expediting access to appropriate agricultural credit is possible . <p> Currently , many formal financial institutions are focusing on offering agricultural credit through the check-off model , collaborating with major off-takers in sectors such as tea , dairy , horticultural exports , and , to a lesser extent , coffee . <h> 3 . Climate change <p> In the 21st century , climate change has had a marked impact on global agriculture . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that most countries are experiencing higher average temperatures , more frequent heat waves , and increasing pressure on water resources . These climate shifts are leading to greater desertification and episodes of intense rainfall . <p> Additionally , the last three decades have been the warmest on record , with each surpassing the previous one . In particular , Africa has become significantly warmer over the past century . With temperatures projected to continue rising and rainfall patterns becoming increasingly erratic , these effects are expected to intensify . <p> In Kenya , where agriculture depends almost entirely ( 98% ) on rainfall , rising temperatures , droughts , and floods leave smallholder farmers especially vulnerable . Semi-arid regions face the threat of becoming fully arid , and many existing arid areas are now too dry to support any agricultural activity . <p> Members of Turkana community joined by climate activists take to the streets of Nairobi and protest for action against climate change . Photo : @James Wakibi ( modified by author ) Source : Getty Images <p> This has also affected sustainable farming in Kenya . Reports show @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ has shrunk . In fact , there has been a 13% reduction in viable grazing lands and a 24% decline in regions suitable for mixed cropping . These changes lead to frequent crop and livestock losses , severely impacting the livelihoods of Kenyan farmers . <h> Has Kenya dealt with severe climate change before ? <p> This wo n't be the first time Kenya has experienced such a situation . Since the early 1990s , Kenya has endured several severe droughts , occurring in 1991 -- 92 , 1992 -- 93 , 1995 -- 96 , 1998 -- 2000 , 2004 , and again in 2008 -- 09 . The El Ni ? o phenomenon also triggered intense rainfall and floods between 1997 and 1998 . <p> Such climate fluctuations and changes , which are gradually taking place in Kenya , will hugely impact agricultural productivity and food security , as a large portion of Kenya 's rural population depends on agriculture for their livelihoods . <p> Limited access to resources and income sources makes smallholder farmers and the rural poor in Kenya particularly susceptible to climate-related and environmental challenges @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ diseases are a significant challenge in Kenya , affecting both the pre-harvest and post-harvest phases due to inadequate storage facilities . For instance , maize stored in the southern regions has been heavily impacted by aflatoxins , resulting in considerable losses . This issue is partially attributed to farmers ' insufficient knowledge of effective pest and disease control . <p> In 2022 , Kenyan agricultural experts raised concerns , claiming that climate change is accelerating the emergence of new pests and diseases . The Agrochemicals Association of Kenya ( AAK ) warned that these pests and diseases are damaging crops and forest ecosystems , endangering food security and the environment . <p> AAK Stewardship Manager Benson Ngigi highlighted some of the most problematic pests , including leaf miners , fruit flies , red spider mites , and larger grain borers , as well as emerging diseases such as anthracnose in beans and avocado , bean spot , maize lethal necrosis , and tomato nematodes . <p> In early 2023 , another issue surfaced : two invasive soil-dwelling fly species were causing extensive damage to vegetable crops . A study by @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of Insect Physiology and Ecology ( ICIPE ) revealed that smallholder farmers struggle with effective control methods . <p> The study , conducted in five counties -- Nyandarua , Nakuru , Kiambu , Kajiado , and Nyeri -- showed that pests are a serious threat to agriculture , especially vegetable production . The researchers also detected other soil-borne pests like white grubs , wireworms , and sap beetles across various agroecological zones . <h> 5 . Soil nutrients <p> Soil nutrition is essential for agriculture , yet access to point-of-need testing is limited in resource-constrained areas in Kenya . For context , in sub-Saharan Africa , over 350 million hectares suffer from soil malnutrition , particularly low levels of nitrogen and phosphorus , impacting Kenya 's agriculture by stunting productivity . <p> Kenyan soils are often deficient in key nutrients such as nitrogen , phosphorus , and sometimes potassium . These nutrients are not naturally replenished , and their depletion is worsened by both agricultural practices and climate change . <p> According to Kavita , the agronomist , there is a significant awareness gap on soil health practices and the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ aligns with the crops planted . <p> " Soil health is another area where significant gaps exist . Many farmers are unaware of their soil 's condition or the importance of soil testing . As a result , soils in high farming areas are often severely depleted , and soil-borne pathogens accumulate . Unfortunately , most farmers are not familiar with methods for addressing soil depletion or eliminating pathogens , including simple practices like crop rotation , " Kavita said . <p> Kenya 's diverse soil types mean fertilisers beneficial in one area may be harmful in another . As a result , some agricultural zones become highly acidic after prolonged fertiliser use . <h> Government policies and initiatives <p> The Kenyan government has continuously sought to address the myriad challenges facing the agricultural sector through various initiatives , including Kenya agricultural development programs , the introduction of bills , policies , and other projects . While some of these efforts have yielded positive results , many have fallen short of their intended goals , leaving farmers grappling with persistent issues . <p> That said , below is the progress @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 1 . The government 's efforts in promoting technology in Kenya <p> The agricultural sector in Kenya has been through an immense technological transformation in recent years , primarily due to the rising adoption of innovations . Key developments in Agri-tech , such as mobile applications , precision farming techniques , and data analytics , have fundamentally altered farming practices . <p> Although the government 's initiatives are still in progress , their impact has been recognized and appreciated . In 2023 , the World Bank collaborated with the Kenyan government to implement digital technology solutions to enhance agricultural productivity . <p> The Ministry of Agriculture , Livestock , Fisheries , and Co-operatives established a Big Data Platform and the Kenya Agricultural Observatory Platform ( KAOP ) through the Kenya Agriculture Livestock and Research Organization ( KALRO ) . This initiative successfully connected 1.1 million farmers to these platforms , offering vital data , information , and agronomic advice . <p> These resources provided access to high-resolution geospatial agro-meteorological data and tailored guidance for national and county agricultural institutions , farmers , and other stakeholders . <h> The One Million @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Million Farmer Platform in partnership with the World Bank , cultivating collaboration between county governments and agricultural technology ( AgTech ) startups to improve service delivery in rural areas . <p> The World Bank 's involvement extended to providing significant technical assistance at various levels of government . An Innovation Challenge , co-hosted by the World Bank and the Ministry of Agriculture , aimed to identify AgTech startups using digital technologies to boost farmers ' productivity and profitability . <p> Innovative solutions included mobile applications offering extension services and credit to farmers , tech platforms facilitating market access , and applications enabling farmers to procure quality inputs like seeds and fertilisers . However , according to Kavita , many farmers are still using traditional seeds which further limits agricultural production in the country . <p> " In terms of seed selection , many farmers are still relying on traditional methods of seed preservation and planting . They are also hesitant to adopt hybrid seeds due to a lack of information on their benefits and the differences between these seeds and GMO seeds which are not largely loved in the country @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ farmers continue to use outdated practices . For example , professional propagators now use advanced propagation methods like soilless mediums and controlled environments to produce healthier seedlings , but many farmers still rely on traditional nurseries , resulting in lower germination rates and weaker seedlings , " Kavita opined. <h> 2 . Promoting different funding options for farmers <p> For a long time , the country has relied heavily on international aid for Kenyan agriculture . However , the government has tried solving the problem before it 's too late . For instance , it signed the Tea Act , 2020 into law . <p> This act introduced the Tea Fund , a price stabilisation initiative aimed at safeguarding the earnings of tea farmers in Kenya when market prices decline . This fund is overseen by the Tea Board of Kenya ( TBK ) and is financed through levies collected from the tea industry , supplemented by government contributions . <p> Additionally , the Act established the Tea Research Foundation , which focuses on prioritising and coordinating tea research across the country . This foundation also provides the government with @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <h> Loans <p> The government also tries to address challenges facing Kenyan farmers in accessing loans . For example , in August 2024 , the state-owned Kenya Development Corporation ( KDC ) allocated over Ksh 300 million in low-cost credit to the Murang'a Farmers Sacco , AMICA . <p> This Sacco will then offer loans to farmers ranging from Ksh 7,000 to Ksh 250,000 at single-digit interest rates . This funding alleviates the financial pressure from private lenders , whose growth has been slow in recent years . <p> Representatives from both the government and AMICA receive the funding . To ensure that farmers have sufficient supplies for upcoming planting seasons , in March 2024 , the government authorised the importation of 12.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser . <p> Even with its efforts , the government still falls short of fully alleviating the fertiliser issue in the country . Combating climate change <p> In addition to government programs for rural farming in Kenya , the government has prioritised climate action , implementing various initiatives to address environmental challenges . A cornerstone of these efforts is the National Climate Change Response Strategy ( NCCRS ) , which aims to promote nationwide engagement in climate adaptation and mitigation . <p> This strategy addresses the vulnerabilities of Kenya 's natural , ecological , and social systems by involving the entire nation in climate action . <p> Environmental protection is also a central component of Kenya 's Vision 2030 -- its long-term development plan spanning from 2008 to 2030 -- and the National Climate Change Action Plan ( 2013 -- 2017 ) , both of which outline specific goals for managing the country 's impact of climate change . <p> One such measure is the Galana Kulalu irrigation scheme , launched in January 2014 in the Tana River region to support agricultural resilience . The project aims to reduce climate change impact by enhancing food security through expanded irrigation . <h> Kenya 's future climate change plans <p> Despite contributing @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ updated its Nationally Determined Contribution ( NDC ) in December 2020 with a pledge to cut emissions by 32% by 2030 compared to business-as-usual projections , aligning with its sustainable development objectives . <h> 4 . The government 's efforts in combating pests and diseases <p> Pests and diseases are a growing threat not only within Kenya but also globally . In recent years , Kenya has faced an increase in pest invasion largely due to the cross-border movement of plants , plant materials , and other items that may carry pests , along with the impacts of climate change . <p> To combat these issues , the Kenyan government enforces the Plant Protection Act ( Cap . 324 ) , a law designed to curb the spread of plant diseases and ensure plant health nationwide . The act criminalises the intentional introduction of pests or diseases onto cultivated land . It also grants the government authority to regulate the import and export of potentially contaminated articles that could introduce such threats . <h> Pests and diseases in livestock <p> The government supports livestock disease management by organising vaccination programs @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of a global initiative to eliminate the Peste des Petits Ruminants ( PPR ) -- a severe viral disease affecting sheep and goats -- the U.S. government , through USAID , partnered with Kenya to develop better strategies for identifying and vaccinating high-risk herds . <p> This USAID-Kenya initiative vaccinated 750,000 sheep and goats in Turkana and Pokot Counties between December 2021 and January 2022 . <p> Preventing PPR is crucial to safeguarding pastoral livelihoods . In Turkana County alone , PPR-related losses due to livestock deaths were estimated at $19 million in 2010 . The vaccine protects animals for life , helping to reduce livestock mortality and improve income stability for pastoral communities . <h> 5 . Efforts in improving soil fertility <p> Soil fertility remains a neglected area in government policy , with limited initiatives to enhance it . Most responsibility for improving soil quality has fallen to farmers and private stakeholders within the agricultural sector . <p> However , despite minimal government involvement , introducing the National Agricultural Soil Management Policy ( NASMP ) in 2023 was a huge step . The NASMP , developed with input @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the essential services soils provide and the pressures they face . <p> The NASMP has specific objectives , including boosting agricultural productivity , strengthening food security , and reducing poverty . Additionally , it aims to protect soil and water resources for future generations . <p> Key aspects of the policy include its recognition of the link between soil management and environmental sustainability , particularly concerning climate change . It also emphasises the role of research and technological advancement in implementing effective soil management practices . <p> Furthermore , it addresses the challenges in fertiliser development and the need for investment to improve soil fertility and crop yields . Collaboration among stakeholders , especially those focused on natural resource management , is highlighted as crucial to the policy 's success . <p> While the Kenyan government has made strides in addressing the challenges faced by the agricultural sector , the effectiveness of these initiatives remains a point of contention among farmers . Many still express concerns about the adequacy and accessibility of support systems , particularly regarding funding , technology adoption , and climate resilience . <p> As agriculture remains @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ imperative for the government to prioritise the needs of farmers and ensure that policies translate into tangible benefits . The future of agriculture in Kenya hangs in the balance . Without sustained efforts to empower farmers and address systemic challenges , the sector may struggle to recover from its current predicaments . <p> Only time will tell if the current policies can rescue agriculture before it 's too late . Still , immediate and comprehensive actions are needed to safeguard the livelihoods of millions who depend on this essential industry . <h> Final word <p> Kenya 's agricultural sector stands at a critical juncture , facing numerous challenges that threaten its sustainability and the livelihoods of millions of farmers . Despite government efforts to implement policies to revitalise the sector , many farmers remain disillusioned due to persistent issues such as outdated technology , inadequate funding , climate change impacts , pest infestations , and soil nutrient depletion . <p> Tuko also published an article detailing why Agriculture is the backbone of the Kenyan economy .
